chapter_name: The Mathematics of 'Maybe': Introduction to Probability
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to measure chance! Understand how mathematics helps us predict the likelihood of random events, from tossing coins to drawing cards.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Probability is the measure of how likely an event is to happen. It is always a number between 0 (Impossible) and 1 (100% Certain). A 0.5 probability means there is a 50-50 chance, like tossing a coin.

The basic formula for probability is: $P(E) = \frac{\text{Number of Favourable Outcomes}}{\text{Total Number of Possible Outcomes}}$. If you want to roll a '4' on a 6-sided die, there is 1 favourable outcome out of 6 possible outcomes, so $P = 1/6$.

Theoretical probability is what we *expect* to happen (like getting Heads 50% of the time). Experimental probability is what *actually* happens when we perform the experiment (like tossing a coin 10 times and getting 7 Heads).

fun_activity.title: 🪙 The Coin Toss Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Toss a coin 10 times and record the number of Heads and Tails. Calculate the 'experimental probability' of your tosses. Then, toss it 50 times. You will notice that the more you toss, the closer your result gets to the theoretical probability of 0.5!

exam_tips: 📌 The sum of the probabilities of all possible outcomes of an experiment is ALWAYS exactly 1.
📌 Probability can NEVER be a negative number, and it can NEVER be greater than 1.
📌 'Equally likely outcomes' means every result has the exact same chance of happening, like a fair die or an unbiased coin.
quick_recap: ⭐ Probability measures the mathematical likelihood of an event occurring.
⭐ It is calculated by dividing favourable outcomes by the total possible outcomes.
